newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London closed lower following a sell-off in the New York raws market, which had opened higher. The sudden trend reversal prompted fairly widespread liquidation in both markets. December lost $2.20 to close at $324.90 a tonne, while other active months were between $4.40 and $2.30 lower.

In New York raw sugar futures closed near the day's lows for the fourth consecutive session which saw the most-active March contract fall to its lowest level in three and a half months. It can not be excluded that we now see the downward move, which had been predicted by market analysts for quite some time.

RUSSIA - Russian harvesting operations are lagging behind. The total harvested by September 23 was 119,000 ha (about 12 per cent of the area sown to sugar beet) compared with 357,000 ha at the same date last year. Yields so far are 3 per cent down on last year at 17.4 tonnes per ha but the gap is expected to widen during the course of the campaign.

Final yields are now estimated to reach 15.5 to 16 tonnes per ha or 11 per cent less than last year. Total beet production could be between 16-17.5 million tonnes, 12 per cent less than last year and after 1994 the lowest figure for the last 40 years. Moreover, due to the late harvest the danger of frost damage is greater than last year so that the drop in production could be more pronounced than is expected at present.

INDIA - The Indian government has come under pressure from sugar producers and has apparently at least for the time being given up its plan to totally liberalize the sugar sector. The government had promised to delicense or deregulate the sugar industry as part of a broader liberalization programme but these plans have come under fire from farmers and cooperative sugar factories, as well as some state governments. Now the government said that before any measures will be taken, it would like to examine in depth the implications of deregulation.

POLAND - According to the Central Statistical Office (GUS) Polish sugar beet output in 1996 is likely to reach between 16.50 and 17.30 million tonnes against last year's 13.31 million. The GUS forecast is based on a projected yield of 36.6 to 38.4 tonnes per ha against 34.6 tonnes in 1995 and an area sown to beet of almost 451,000 ha compared to 385,000 ha in 1995.

HUNGARY - Favourable growing conditions have resulted in satisfactory increases in both beet weight and sugar content. Beet weight on September 23 amounted to 856 grams against 659 grams in 1995. Sugar content rose by 0.6 percentage points to 14.1 per cent against 14.3 per cent in 1995. This resulted in a theoretical sugar weight per root of 120.7 grams, almost 31 per cent up on the previous year.

The results suggest that Hungary will have quite a good harvest in 1996 and signs are that overall beet production will not be much changed from 1995 despite the fact that the area sown to beet fell by nearly 10 per cent to 112,000 ha.

SWEDEN - After long delays which were caused by the accession of Sweden to the EU, the first trade figures for calendar year 1995 are now available. According to these data, sugar imports dropped precipitously in 1995 to 7,437 tonnes, raw value, against 77,236 tonnes in calendar year 1994. Major countries of origin in 1995 were the United Kingdom with 3,343 tonnes whites against 2,757 tonnes and Denmark with 1,587 tonnes compared to 244 tonnes.

Sugar exports in 1995 were sharply up at 17,136 tonnes against 11,383 tonnes in 1994. Major countries of destination in 1995 were Russia with 6,049 tonnes whites against 18 tonnes, Germany with 5,502 tonnes compared to 79 tonnes and Lithuania with 3,002 tonnes against nil.

BRAZIL - According to data by the Association of Sugar and Alcohol Industries of Sao Paulo (AIAA), sugar production in the center/south up to September 16 amounted to 7.12 million tonnes, tel quel, 16.2 per cent up on last year's 6.13 million tonnes. Alcohol production in the same period amounted to 8.34 billion litres, 13.8 per cent more than the 7.33 billion litres produced up to September 16, 1995. According to industry sources, total cane output in the center/south in 1996 will be 5 to 8 per cent up on the previous year.
Syria bought one cargo of white sugar at $368.95 per tonne for October 20 - November 20 shipment. Syria originally tendered to buy 13,000 tonnes of whites and 13,000 tonnes of raws.
